chapters.title: Screening fragment — not an edition
paragraphs: There dwelt in Westphalia in the Castle of the Baron de Thunder-ten-tronck, a young Man, whom Nature had blessed with the most engaging Manners. His Aspect was an index to his Soul. His Judgment was pretty good, and Simplicity great: which, I imagine was the Reason of his being called Candidus. The old Servant suspected he was the Son of the Baron’s Sister, and an honest Gentleman in the Neighbourhood, whom the Lady refused to marry, because he could not trace his Pedigree higher than Seventy-one Generations, having lost the Tree of his Genealogy, by the Injury of Time.

The Baron was one of the greatest Lords in all Westphalia; for his Castle had both a Door and Windows to it: Nay, even his great Hall was hung with Tapestry. The Dogs, which kept his Yards, made up his Pack upon occasion; his Hostlers were his Huntsmen, and the Vicar of the Village his grand Almoner. They all stiled him My Lord, and laughed at his Stories.

My Lady, the Baroness, who weighed about Three Hundred and Fifty Pounds, attracted no small notice on that Account, and did the Honours of the House with a Dignity, which rendered her still more respectable. Her Daughter Cunigonda, was Seventeen, of a sanguine Complexion, fresh, lusty and amorous. The Son of the Baron appeared in every respect worthy of his Father. His Preceptor, Pangloss, was the Oracle of the House, and the little Candidus listened to his Lectures with all the Simplicity, that was suitable to his Age and Character.
